create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

oidc_jwt.description: Externally issued JWTs used for machine-to-machine JWT authentication are documented as being checked for signature by selected source certificates and exp freshness, with no documented jti replay tracking.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same valid external JWT may succeed by design; do not flag as replay vulnerability absent stronger one-time semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive an access token by default; refresh tokens require offline_access to be configured and requested.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Authorization code / Refresh token grant
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of refresh_token is not a bug unless offline_access was both configured and requested.

oidc_jwt.description: When a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing scope can broaden returned claims by design; always request explicit scopes in authorization tests.

oidc_jwt.description: The email scope now defaults email_verified to False unless customized by a scope mapping.
oidc_jwt.note: Applications expecting email_verified=true may fail by design unless a custom mapping is configured.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT authentication creates a service account based on the provider name and the subject claim of the token.
oidc_jwt.note: Granted identity may be provider-scoped service-account metadata rather than a raw sub echo.

oidc_jwt.description: Automatically generated service accounts for client_secret-based client_credentials follow the naming scheme ak-<provider_name>-client_credentials.
oidc_jwt.note: A provider-prefixed service account name is expected and should not be treated as identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Redirect URI validation can be configured with regular expressions instead of exact URLs.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs
oidc_jwt.note: Broad redirect acceptance may be administrator-configured behavior, not a validation bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: If an OAuth2 provider's Redirect URI field is left empty, the first URL used when a user opens the app is saved as the redirect URL.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs
oidc_jwt.note: Unexpected acceptance of the first callback URL on an unconfigured provider is documented behavior, not an open redirect bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive an access token by default; refresh tokens are only issued when offline_access is configured and requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing refresh_token is expected unless offline_access is enabled on both sides.

oidc_jwt.description: A provider configured to federate with other authentik providers accepts valid access tokens issued by any configured Federated OIDC Providers.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of a token from another explicitly federated provider is by design, not cross-provider audience bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: A provider configured with trusted OAuth Sources accepts JWTs signed by any of the configured sources' JWKS certificates.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of a JWT from any selected trusted source is expected; tests must isolate trust anchors carefully.

oidc_jwt.description: RP-initiated logout uses default-provider-invalidation-flow, which by default does not include User Logout, so only the application session ends while the authentik session remains active.
oidc_jwt.note: Persistence of the authentik session after application logout is by design unless the flow is customized.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, authentik documents only that input JWTs must have exp not set as now or in the past for external JWTs, and must not have expired for authentik-issued JWTs. The docs do not document nbf or iat enforcement. Always run a CONTROL login in the same setup using a valid JWT with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} so LOGIN_FAILED on the attack token is not misread as broken provider/source configuration.

For I1 trust-anchor and key-rotation tests on login_with_jwt, configure_jwt_validation MUST select the intended Federated OIDC Sources or Federated OIDC Providers on the OAuth2 provider. Authentik accepts any JWT signed by any configured selected source/provider; if multiple trust anchors remain selected, attacker-signed tokens may succeed by design under the broader trust set.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation, authentik states that OAuth Sources fetch discovery/JWKS data upon saving the source and do no automatic re-fetching. After changing Well-known URL or OIDC JWKS URL, the fuzzer MUST force a save/update of the source/provider configuration before retesting. Do not assume runtime JWKS refresh.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, authentik's documented built-in JWT checks for externally issued JWTs are signature by selected source certificates and exp freshness. Issuer restriction is not a dedicated provider parameter in the docs; issuer enforcement must be implemented with an Expression policy over request.context["oauth_jwt"]["iss"]. Without such a policy, forged issuer / trust-anchor-substitution tests are inconclusive and may pass by design.

For I5 audience-binding tests on login_with_jwt, the docs do not describe a dedicated audience restriction parameter for JWT authentication. Audience enforcement must be implemented with an Expression policy over request.context["oauth_jwt"]["aud"]. Without such a policy, cross-provider or wrong-audience acceptance is by configuration, not necessarily a bug.

For I5 claim-binding tests on login_with_jwt, authentik exposes parsed JWT claims to Expression policies as request.context["oauth_jwt"]. Matching semantics are therefore Python-expression-defined, not a documented exact/glob/regex parameterized matcher. The fuzzer MUST implement explicit equality/type checks in policy logic for each test and MUST NOT assume wildcard support or implicit coercion.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on JWT claims, the docs do not specify cross-type comparison behavior for request.context["oauth_jwt"] values. The fuzzer SHOULD test explicit numeric coercion behavior in policy expressions by binding an integer expectation and sending a float value (for example 100 vs 100.7) to detect silent truncation/coercion. Any acceptance depends on the policy expression, not a built-in matcher.

For I4 principal-binding tests on login_with_jwt, authentik creates service accounts for JWT authentication based on the provider name and the subject claim of the input token. Different providers can therefore intentionally namespace identities by provider, and the same sub across different providers need not collide. Cross-provider identity comparisons must account for provider-scoped service account creation.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti on login_with_jwt, do NOT treat repeated use of the same externally issued JWT as a vulnerability by itself. The docs only require signature and expiry checks for external JWTs, and validity/revocation/expiry for authentik-issued JWTs; no jti tracking or one-time-use semantics are documented for generic JWT bearer authentication.

For I2 revocation tests, distinguish input JWT validity from output token revocation. Authentik documents that authentik-issued input JWTs used for JWT authentication must not have been revoked, but externally issued JWTs are only checked for signature and exp. Revoking the output access token via /application/o/revoke/ does not imply the external input JWT becomes unusable.

For I3 config-change sequences, authentik documents that any change made to an outpost-associated app/provider immediately triggers an update event, but OAuth source JWKS/discovery data is only fetched on save and not auto-refreshed. A valid coherence test must compare behavior before and after an explicit config save/update, not expect passive background propagation from remote JWKS changes alone.

Redirect URI validation in authentik can use exact values or regex patterns configured by the administrator. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, ensure the provider is configured with an exact redirect URI when testing strict matching. If regex is configured, broader matches are by design and can cause false positives.

When no scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. For I5 scope-escalation or minimal-scope tests, the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope parameter; omitting scope broadens claims by design and invalidates least-privilege conclusions.

Starting with authentik 2024.2, refresh tokens are only issued when both the application/provider configuration includes offline_access and the request asks for offline_access. Tests that expect refresh_token issuance or revocation MUST include offline_access in both setup and request; absence of refresh_token is otherwise by design.

The authorization code in authentik can only be used once and expires quickly. For I3 code-reuse or code-injection style tests, a second redemption failure is expected behavior and should be asserted via HTTP status/error, not treated as identity mismatch.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, authentik only documents validation of JWT expiration for M2M JWT authentication: external JWTs must have exp not set as now or in the past, and authentik-issued JWTs must not have expired. The docs do not state nbf or iat validation for input JWTs. The fuzzer MUST include a control login using a valid JWT alongside any expired/future-token attack so LOGIN_FAILED can be attributed to token freshness rather than broken setup.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti, do NOT treat repeated use of the same external JWT as a vulnerability by default. The documentation for JWT authentication only requires signature trust and expiration checks for external JWTs, and validity/revocation/expiration for authentik-issued access tokens; it does not document jti tracking or one-time-use semantics for JWT bearer login.

For I1 trust-anchor_substitution and resign_attacker_key tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST restrict accepted signing keys by selecting specific Federated OIDC Sources or Federated OIDC Providers for the target OAuth2 provider. authentik accepts any JWT issued by any configured source/provider certificates. If multiple trust anchors are attached, a token signed by any of them is expected to authenticate and is not evidence of missing signature validation.

For I1 kid_injection tests, use a JWKS containing both benign and attacker-controlled keys only when both keys are actually trusted by the configured source/provider. The documentation states authentik accepts JWTs signed by any of the selected sources' JWKS certificates; acceptance of a JWT signed by a key present in trusted JWKS is by design, not a kid-selection flaw.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, authentik does not document a built-in issuer binding parameter for M2M JWT authentication. Issuer restrictions, if desired, are implemented via Expression policies using request.context["oauth_jwt"]["iss"]. The fuzzer MUST create and bind such a policy when testing issuer enforcement; otherwise acceptance of a mismatched iss is inconclusive because no issuer check was configured.

For I5 audience-binding tests on login_with_jwt, authentik documentation does not describe a dedicated audience restriction parameter for input JWT authentication. Audience and other claim restrictions must be enforced via Expression policies over request.context["oauth_jwt"]. The fuzzer MUST bind an explicit policy checking aud before asserting audience mismatch vulnerabilities; otherwise cross-audience acceptance may simply reflect absent policy.

For I5 claim-binding tests, authentik's documented mechanism is Expression policies over request.context["oauth_jwt"], not declarative bound_claims parameters. Because matching semantics are Python-expression-defined, there is no wildcard or exact-match sentinel to infer from API shape. The fuzzer MUST treat claim restriction behavior as policy-defined and avoid assuming support for wildcard patterns, regexes, or exact-only matching unless the configured expression explicitly implements them.

For I5 numeric claim coercion tests, the docs do not specify cross-type comparison semantics for request.context["oauth_jwt"] claim values. The fuzzer SHOULD explicitly test numeric coercion in Expression policies by comparing an integer policy value against a float JWT claim (for example 100 vs 100.7) and determine whether authentik or the policy logic coerces or truncates values unexpectedly. Any result depends on the expression used, not a documented built-in matcher.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, note that OAuth Source discovery and JWKS fetching occur when the source is saved and no automatic re-fetching is done. After changing a source's Well-known URL or OIDC JWKS URL, the fuzzer MUST re-save/update the source/provider configuration before expecting new keys to take effect. Otherwise continued acceptance of old keys may reflect stale cached JWKS, not a coherence bug.

For I3 config-change sequences involving sources embedded in flows, authentik Source stage suspends the current flow and resumes it later using a dynamic in-memory stage. If the configured source's authentication or enrollment flow contains a User Login stage, the original flow will not resume and the pending user is directly authenticated. The fuzzer MUST avoid such source-flow configurations when testing flow coherence, or results will be invalid by design.

For I3 redirect/state-style OIDC tests, start_oidc_auth returns redirects and must be executed with redirect following disabled. The executor MUST preserve and correlate state/nonce across the browser-mediated flow; otherwise failures may be caused by client-side redirect handling rather than authentik's session binding.

For I3 PKCE tests, exchange_code_for_token uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests at /application/o/token/. The fuzzer MUST send code_verifier only in the token request and code_challenge/code_challenge_method only in the authorization request. Mixing parameters across steps can create false negatives unrelated to PKCE enforcement.

For I5 scope-escalation tests, authentik treats requests with no scopes as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. Therefore the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit limited scope set in baseline and attack requests. Omitting scope does not mean minimal privilege; it broadens requested claims by design.

For refresh-token expectations in exchange_code_for_token, starting with authentik 2024.2 applications only receive an access token unless both the application/provider and the request include offline_access. The fuzzer MUST not treat absence of refresh_token as a bug unless offline_access was configured and requested.

For introspect_token tests, authentik documents that a token can only be introspected from the same provider that was used to authenticate, unless it is first exchanged for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection requests in the same provider context or perform a prior token exchange; cross-provider introspection failure is by design.

For redirect_uri validation tests, authentik validates redirect URIs against the provider's configured Redirect URI list. If the Redirect URI field is left empty when creating a new OAuth2 provider/application, the first URL a user opens for that app is saved as the redirect URL. The fuzzer MUST preconfigure explicit redirect URIs for deterministic redirect_uri_mismatch testing; otherwise first-use auto-saving can mask or alter validation behavior.

Redirect URI matching supports regular expressions when configured by the administrator. The fuzzer MUST distinguish exact redirect URI entries from regex-based entries when testing redirect_uri_mismatch. Acceptance of multiple callback URLs under a configured regex is by design, not necessarily an authorization flaw.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the input JWT is only documented to be checked for signature trust and exp freshness. The docs do not state nbf or iat validation for JWT M2M authentication. The fuzzer MUST include a control login using a valid JWT alongside any attack JWT and MUST treat nbf/iat results as implementation-dependent unless explicitly observed.

For I1 trust-anchor tests on login_with_jwt, configure_jwt_validation MUST select Federated OIDC Sources via Well-known URL, OIDC JWKS URL, or raw JWKS data. Without selecting trusted sources on the OAuth2 provider, JWT signature validation is not configured and any failure is ambiguous.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source -> JWKS; Machine-to-Machine (M2M) authentication -> Externally issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 claim-constraint tests on login_with_jwt, authentik exposes parsed JWT claims to Expression policies as request.context["oauth_jwt"]. There is no documented companion matching-mode parameter such as bound_claims_type. Matching semantics are therefore policy-defined, not platform-fixed. The fuzzer MUST implement exact, wildcard, or coercion behavior explicitly in the policy under test and MUST NOT assume wildcard support from configuration alone.

For I5 numeric claim coercion tests on login_with_jwt, the docs do not specify cross-type comparison semantics for Expression policies over request.context["oauth_jwt"]. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly in policy logic by comparing an integer bound value against a float claim (for example N vs N+0.7) and determine whether policy evaluation truncates, coerces, or rejects. Do not assume stringification or exact numeric typing without measurement.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti on externally issued JWTs, authentik only documents signature trust and exp freshness checks for input JWTs. No jti tracking or one-time-use semantics are documented. Reuse of the same valid external JWT is therefore a hardening check at most, not a vulnerability by itself.

For I2 replay tests on authentik-issued JWTs used as input to login_with_jwt, the docs state that input JWTs must not have been revoked and must not have expired. The fuzzer MUST revoke the authentik-issued subject token before asserting replay rejection based on revocation; otherwise repeated use of an unrevoked valid token may be by design.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, OAuth Sources fetch discovery/JWKS data upon saving and no automatic re-fetching is done. After changing Well-known or JWKS configuration, the fuzzer MUST save/update the source/provider configuration before retesting. Do not assume background refresh of trust anchors.

For I3 config-change sequences involving flows or source stages, authentik can evaluate policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. A valid coherence test MUST ensure the same request is not merely being re-planned under new config. Config changes affecting new logins are by design; stale behavior must be shown within the same logical request/session context to claim an I3 issue.

For OIDC request-object tests (oidc_request_object_alg_none), the authorization endpoint accepts an optional request JWT parameter per OIDC. The docs do not specify request object signature enforcement settings. The fuzzer SHOULD test unsigned request objects directly at start_oidc_auth, but MUST interpret acceptance cautiously unless client-side request object signing requirements are explicitly configured elsewhere.
oidc_jwt.source: Required canonical OIDC extraction rule; Authorization endpoint glossary

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC code-flow tests, redirect_uri validation is strict against the provider's configured Redirect URI list. If the Redirect URI field is empty, authentik saves the first URL used when the app is first opened. The fuzzer MUST preconfigure explicit redirect URIs for deterministic tests and MUST NOT rely on first-use auto-save during security testing.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Redirect URI matching supports regular expressions when configured by the admin. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether the provider uses literal URI entries or regex entries. A broad regex can intentionally allow multiple callbacks; acceptance under such config is by design, not a bug.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Refresh tokens are only issued when both the application/provider configuration includes offline_access and the request asks for offline_access. The fuzzer MUST request offline_access explicitly and ensure the provider is configured for it before expecting refresh_token behavior from exchange_code_for_token.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Authorization code; Create an OAuth2 provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: Authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. For I3 code-injection or reuse tests, the fuzzer MUST capture and reuse the exact same code value and assert rejection on second redemption. Failures after a long delay may be simple expiry, not replay protection.

For PKCE-related OIDC tests, authentik documents PKCE support but does not state it is mandatory for all clients. The fuzzer SHOULD treat missing PKCE enforcement as a hardening check unless the client is explicitly configured to require it, and should assert non-200 status on exchange failures rather than compare identities.

For OIDC SSO id_token validation tests where authentik acts as RP via OAuth Sources, the docs describe OIDC-compatible profile retrieval and configurable authorization/token/JWKS URLs but do not explicitly enumerate nonce, aud, iss, and exp checks. The fuzzer MUST include control logins and test each claim separately; any rejection/acceptance must be interpreted as observed behavior, not assumed from docs.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source; Entra ID OAuth authentication

oidc_jwt.constraint: For cross-provider JWT audience tests, each OAuth2 provider has its own client_id and JWT authentication is performed against the selected provider. The fuzzer MUST create two distinct providers/applications and present the same JWT to both. Acceptance at provider B is only meaningful if provider B is configured to trust the same federated source/provider as A; otherwise failure may be due to trust configuration, not audience enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine (M2M) authentication -> Externally issued JWTs; OAuth 2.0 provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: The OAuth introspection endpoint only allows introspection of a token from the same provider used to authenticate, unless the token is first exchanged into that provider. The fuzzer MUST introspect with matching provider credentials or perform token exchange first; cross-provider introspection failures are by design.

For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use token_exchange at /application/o/token/ only if the target application/provider is configured for federation between providers. Without configured federated providers, rejection is expected and does not prove audience enforcement.

For login_with_jwt using Entra-issued tokens, the upstream token request to Entra must use scope=api://<application_client_id>/.default rather than Graph scopes, otherwise the JWT format is invalid for authentik. The fuzzer MUST mint control tokens with the Application ID URI scope before testing authentik acceptance/rejection.
oidc_jwt.source: Entra ID OAuth authentication -> Machine-to-machine authentication

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
